# mtncloud_mos_access (Resource)

The tenant's MOS (MTN Object Storage) keys. MOS has one pair of keys per tenant, kept in Cypher. Create **adopts** the keys the tenant already has and orders nothing; it orders the MOS catalog item only when the tenant has no keys, or when `rotate = true`. Changing `rotate_trigger` orders new keys in place. **Ordering replaces the keys for the whole tenant:** every tool and user of the old keys loses access until it takes the new ones from Cypher (MTN's workflow updates the console's own bucket records). The keys are never stored in state: MOS resources read them from Cypher. Destroy deletes nothing: the keys stay, since others use them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Adopts the tenant's MOS keys, or orders them if the tenant has none.
resource "mtncloud_mos_access" "keys" {}

# To rotate the keys later, for the whole tenant, change the trigger:
#
# resource "mtncloud_mos_access" "keys" {
#   rotate_trigger = "2026-11"
# }

# Buckets made in the same apply wait for the keys.
resource "mtncloud_mos_bucket" "logs" {
  name       = "acme-logs"
  depends_on = [mtncloud_mos_access.keys]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `rotate` (Boolean) Order new keys at create even when the tenant has keys, which replaces them for the whole tenant. Only used at create; to rotate later, change `rotate_trigger`. Defaults to `false`: adopt.
- `rotate_trigger` (String) Any value. Changing it from one value to another, once the resource exists, orders new keys in place, replacing them for the whole tenant (for example a date: `rotate_trigger = "2026-11"`). Setting it where it was unset (at create, or after an import) and removing it rotate nothing. A value known only at apply may rotate: the plan says so.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Where the keys are in Cypher: `secret/MOS-<tenant>_<user>_` (no secret).
- `order_id` (String) The catalog order that made the keys, when this resource ordered them; empty when adopted.
- `private_endpoint` (String) MOS endpoint from inside MTN Cloud.
- `public_endpoint` (String) MOS endpoint from the internet.
- `source` (String) `adopted` (the tenant's keys, nothing ordered) or `ordered` (this resource ordered them last).

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A tenant has one pair of MOS keys: any ID adopts them.
terraform import mtncloud_mos_access.keys mos
```
